purpose: Builds the final child environment with ordered overrides and platform name rules.
behavior: Inherited values are copied unless disabled; clean Windows environment retains one normalized SystemRoot before caller overrides/removals.
Each override removes every equivalent name then optionally inserts its new value; no interpolation is performed.
Unix names compare exactly; Windows folds individual UTF-16 units using one-to-one BMP uppercase, preserving surrogates and expansion-only case mappings.
contracts: Environment lookup uses the same name-equivalence function as merge.
dependencies: spawn::prepare uses build; resolve reads child PATH/PATHEXT from the resulting vector.
failures_or_limits: Windows ordinal behavior is emulated through Rust Unicode casing rather than calling CompareStringOrdinal; exact equivalence across all OS Unicode table versions is not established here.

purpose: Defines unchecked requests and resolved launch specifications plus preparation order.
behavior: Request defaults to inherited environment, pipes, closed stdin, separate stderr, two-second grace and no timeout/RSS/verbatim options.
prepare validates fields, merges environment, validates absolute cwd, resolves executable on final child PATH, then rejects verbatim batch targets.
Spec keeps resolved executable separately from literal caller argv[0] and carries fully materialized environment and cwd to the supervisor.
contracts: Preparation starts no process; timeout and memory enforcement belong to process layer.
dependencies: spawn/env, validate and resolve implement the three transformations; client/start encodes Spec.
failures_or_limits: The module calls environment/filesystem queries despite its pure/no-execution description; it is not referentially pure.

evidence.quote:
impl Request {
    pub(crate) fn new(program: OsString) -> Request {
        Request {
            program,
            args: Vec::new(),
            cwd: None,
            env: Vec::new(),
            inherit_env: true,
            mode: Mode::Pipe,
            stdin: Stdin::Closed,
            merge_stderr: false,
            grace: DEFAULT_GRACE,
            timeout: None,
            max_rss_bytes: None,
            verbatim: None,
        }

purpose: Implements OS-parameterized path classification, joining and PATH splitting.
behavior: Distinguishes absolute, root-relative, drive-relative and relative Windows paths; drive-relative joins return None.
Root-relative Windows paths reuse the base drive; normal relatives append a separator while verbatim bases use platform Path joining.
PATH drops empty entries; Windows uses semicolons with removable double quotes, Unix colons; extension detection examines the last component.
contracts: No implicit current directory is introduced by empty PATH components.
dependencies: resolve uses join/split/extension; validate uses kind for cwd and command refusal.
failures_or_limits: UNC/verbatim-base fallback uses host Path semantics and is exact only on Windows for those cases. Unbalanced PATH quotes are tolerated by the splitter.

purpose: Resolves commands using final child environment and classified filesystem outcomes.
behavior: Bare names search child PATH in order; separator paths resolve against child cwd and skip PATH. Empty and drive-relative PATH entries do not imply cwd.
Windows uses PATHEXT or .COM;.EXE;.BAT;.CMD, tries an explicit extension first, and accepts only exe/com/bat/cmd as startable.
Missing/non-directory candidates are skipped, inaccessible/nonexecutable candidates are remembered, and unrelated filesystem failures immediately become Io.
contracts: Returns first runnable candidate; if none, first concrete execution refusal outranks NotFound.
dependencies: env name lookup and path rules provide platform semantics; spawn/sys checks Unix execute permission.
failures_or_limits: Metadata and execution are separate, so later changes still require supervisor exec failure handling.

purpose: Performs Unix executable-access checks while avoiding libc paths that can fork the host.
behavior: Normal equal real/effective IDs use faccessat X_OK with flags zero; EACCES becomes false, other errors propagate.
For differing IDs, checks only regular-file status and any execute bit, leaving actual permission decision to supervisor execve.
contracts: Deliberately avoids AT_EACCESS because musl can fork a helper for that mode.
dependencies: spawn/resolve::probe calls can_execute after path resolution; libc provides identity/access syscalls.
failures_or_limits: Setuid/setgid preflight is intentionally approximate; successful preflight does not guarantee exec success.

purpose: Tests environment and validation rules under both OS models plus real preparation filesystem checks.
behavior: Verifies ordered override/removal, clean-env SystemRoot retention, case-sensitive Unix versus UTF-16-unit Windows names including lone surrogates and nonexpanding folds.
Invalid NUL/key/size/duration inputs must name fields, hide secret-bearing values and precede missing-cwd/program errors.
Cwd tests cover relative, absolute, UNC/root-relative and rejected drive-relative paths; real Unix permission search skips owner-denied files and Windows resolves npm.cmd over extensionless npm.
contracts: Nothing is executed by these tests; files and directories serve as resolution inputs.
dependencies: spawn/env, validate, sys and prepare are implementation targets.
failures_or_limits: Windows-specific preparation checks run only on Windows; parameterized rules alone do not establish native execution.

purpose: Exercises resolution precedence and filesystem error classification with injected probe results.
behavior: First runnable PATH candidate wins; earlier directories/nonexecutables/permission failures are skipped but reported if no later executable exists.
No PATH, empty PATH and missing candidates yield precise NotFound messages; unexpected probe error is Io rather than missing.
Windows cases honor PATHEXT, refuse nonstartable extensions, resolve root-relative names against child drive, skip drive-relative PATH entries and preserve quoted semicolons.
contracts: Drive-relative commands fail before the probe is invoked.
dependencies: spawn/resolve::find receives a fake filesystem and both OS rule sets.
failures_or_limits: This verifies algorithm decisions and probe order, not real filesystem permissions or Windows process startup.

purpose: Pins verbatim-tail refusal rules, batch normalization and secret-safe diagnostics.
behavior: Windows accepts an empty or arbitrary non-NUL tail alone; Unix and simultaneous argv reject InvalidArgument.
NUL-tail error must identify byte seven without echoing the supplied token.
Batch checks cover case, trailing dots/spaces, verbatim prefixes and slash variants, while explicit cmd.exe and similarly named nonbatch targets remain eligible.
contracts: Unix prepare refuses verbatim before trying to resolve a nonexistent executable.
failures_or_limits: Passing validation does not assert arbitrary cmd.exe syntax is safe or portable.

purpose: Validates launch fields before resolution and establishes an accessible directory.
behavior: Checks empty/NUL command, drive-relative Windows program, NUL argv/cwd/env, malformed env names, verbatim conflicts, PTY range and duration range in deterministic order.
Verbatim batch refusal strips trailing dots/spaces from final component before case-insensitive bat/cmd detection.
Absolute cwd bypasses host-cwd lookup; relative/root-relative uses host cwd, drive-relative is rejected; metadata distinguishes missing/nondirectory/inaccessible.
contracts: Timeout/grace validation rounds fractional milliseconds upward for bounds, but does not rewrite Request durations.
dependencies: spawn/path determines path kind; error/messages/w03 and wp8b produce errors.
failures_or_limits: The header says before any syscall, but cwd/directory helpers perform filesystem calls after syntactic check. Grace wire conversion elsewhere should be checked for fractional-duration consistency.

purpose: Defines dependency-light public values shared across every host layer.
behavior: Stdin defaults Closed; PtySize defaults 80x24; Data distinguishes replacement-decoded text from raw bytes, although Display decodes bytes lossily.
Chunk/Line attach per-stream loss metadata; Line continues marks all but last piece over 1 MiB; PTY drops count as stdout.
Exit carries unsigned native code, optional Unix signal and explicit reason including MemoryExceeded; success requires ordinary Exit code zero. ProcessInfo only links parents inside the same list.
contracts: Nonexhaustive structs permit future fields; Windows codes remain nonnegative u32 and signals are absent.
dependencies: api reexports these values; error result and process/io modules consume them.
failures_or_limits: RunOutput complete-output wording also appears in partial error results; callers must inspect the enclosing Result/error contract.

purpose: Runs all applicable JSON conformance scenarios through the Rust public API with explicit pending accounting.
behavior: Requires built fixture/supervisor binaries, warms the fixture, reads pending.txt and drives runner::suite on a four-worker runtime.
Prints passed/pending/failed totals and requires ran+other to equal all scenario files.
Only suite errors fail the test; expected product failures in the pending ledger may remain pending.
contracts: Missing binaries fail rather than skip; supervisor environment override is set before runner threads.
dependencies: tests/runner implements scenario selection/classification; conformance/scenarios and pending.txt define inputs.
failures_or_limits: A successful suite can still contain pending product failures; no current execution totals are claimed here.
